scorecard.name: Hold time and Dead Air
scorecard.coaching: At [04:07]-[04:51] and [06:17]-[07:06], formally ask to place the customer on hold and thank him upon returning rather than leaving two unmanaged dead-air gaps of 34s and 39s after casual remarks.

scorecard.name: Active listening
scorecard.coaching: At [07:38], pay attention to details the customer already shared earlier—Maximilian clearly stated at [01:55] that he was browsing from Safari on his MacBook Pro.

grader.scenario: Admin GUI login rejecting factory card password on S-Net Hub 4 and disabling WPS push-button after security audit warning
grader.notes: Ross handles verification ([01:26]-[01:43]), empathy ([00:21]), paraphrasing ([00:58]), diagnostic probing ([02:03]-[02:40]), and live resolution verification ([08:20]-[10:46]) well, but fails Hold/Dead Air with two near-threshold unmanaged gaps of 34s ([04:07]-[04:51]) and 39s ([06:17]-[07:06]) and fails Active Listening at [07:38] by asking which browser and OS Maximilian is using after he stated 'Safari on my MacBook Pro' at [01:55].

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: [00:00] Ross opens with 'thank you for calling S-Net' and closes at [11:44] with 'Thank you for choosing S-Net'.

items.name: Hold time and Dead Air
items.evidence: [04:07]-[04:51] (34s unmanaged gap after 'Just a sec while I check the TR-069 management console') and [06:17]-[07:06] (39s unmanaged gap after 'Hold on while that syncs'), both exceeding the 30-second threshold without formal hold announcements or return thank-yous.

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: [01:26]-[01:43] Ross verifies Maximilian's Edinburgh address, postcode, four-digit PIN, and security question well within the first 240 seconds.

items.name: Personalized the call/ticket appropriately
items.evidence: [00:21] Ross addresses Maximilian by name throughout the call.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: [00:21] Ross apologizes for the frustration and hassle and validates Maximilian's urgency around passing his employer's home-working security audit.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: [00:58] Ross clearly paraphrases both parts of Maximilian's request: resolving the S-Net Hub 4 admin GUI rejecting the 12-character pull-out card password, and disabling WPS so his network passes his workplace security audit.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: [01:55] Maximilian explicitly states 'I'm sitting right next to the router browsing from Safari on my MacBook Pro', but at [07:38] Ross asks 'and which web browser and operating system are you using to open 192.168.1.1?'

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: [00:45], [03:45]-[07:06], [08:46]-[10:15] Ross takes full ownership of resetting the Web GUI password hash via TR-069 without wiping Maximilian's NAS port-forwarding rules, walking him through disabling WPS, and locking the hardware button.

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: [00:21]-[11:44] Ross maintains a warm, helpful, and collaborative tone throughout.

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: [02:03]-[02:40], [05:25]-[05:43] Ross asks targeted diagnostic probing questions about the login prompt fields, case sensitivity, whether the Hub 4 was migrated from an older Hub 3 via cloud backup, and LED status.

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: [08:20]-[10:46] Maximilian logs into `192.168.1.1` using the factory card password ([08:20]), confirms his 6 NAS port-forwarding rules are intact ([08:37]), disables WPS across 2.4GHz and 5GHz ([09:43]), and confirms his employer's security scanner reports 'PASS — WPS Disabled on BSSID' ([10:46]).
